title: How kidneys regulate blood and make urine
intro: The kidneys filter blood, adjust water and salts and help maintain acid balance. They also support blood-pressure control, red-cell production and bone health. Making urine is only part of their work; normal urine volume does not prove normal kidney function.

sections.heading: Filtering units
paragraphs: Small units called nephrons filter fluid from blood, then selectively return needed water and substances. Waste leaves in urine through the ureters to the bladder. Urine is not simply untreated blood with cells removed.

sections.heading: Balance and hormones
paragraphs: Kidneys respond to body signals to conserve or remove water and salts. They release signals involved in pressure and red-cell production and activate vitamin D. Disease can therefore affect several systems before obvious urinary symptoms appear.

sections.heading: Checking function
paragraphs: Blood creatinine-based estimates and urine tests, including albumin when appropriate, answer complementary questions. Results need context and sometimes repetition. A single estimate or home dipstick cannot explain every kidney problem.

sections.heading: Protecting kidneys
paragraphs: Manage blood pressure and diabetes with advice, avoid smoking and check medicines that may harm kidneys. Drinking excessive water does not cleanse damaged kidneys; fluid advice differs in heart failure or advanced kidney disease.

sections.heading: Warning signs
paragraphs: Visible blood, new swelling or persistent urinary changes deserve assessment. Very little urine with illness, severe dehydration, fever with flank pain or major breathlessness needs urgent help. Early chronic kidney disease can be silent, so indicated checks still matter when well. Before a consultation, note when a symptom began, what makes it better or worse, and how it affects ordinary activities. Bring previous reports if available. Ask the professional to connect the explanation to your own findings rather than assuming that a general description establishes a diagnosis.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira passes urine normally but has diabetes. She attends recommended blood and urine checks rather than assuming volume proves healthy filtering.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben asks before using repeated anti-inflammatory tablets because his kidney function is reduced, instead of treating an over-the-counter label as proof of safety.
